chunks: And by his chain, from Ali (peace be upon him), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
I was ordered to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God; and when they say it, their blood and property become sacred to me.

key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but God (Shahadah)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the protection of a person's life and property in Islamic tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, establishes the Shahadah as the primary criterion for the cessation of hostilities, reflecting the Shia understanding of the Prophet's political and military authority. It underscores that the protection of life and wealth is contingent upon the public declaration of faith, a principle central to the concept of *Jihad* as a means of inviting to Islam rather than forced conversion. The narration highlights the transition from the state of war to the state of peace based on this verbal testimony.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-281 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ali (a.s.)
the Prophet (S) said, “I was ordered to fight with the people until they declared There is no god but God and then their lives and property was secured.”
